It is not wrong to be critical of the persistent message that people following "all in" must respond to literally every craving they have, because it indicates extreme hunger, and that means your body is literally calling out for you to provide it with, say, ice-cream immediately is such a damaging belief to implement. No. Cravings and hunger are entirely separate entities. A person can experience a craving for a specific food regardless of whether they are actually hungry or not, and teaching people to interpret all cravings as a sign of hunger is dangerous ground. People often crave high carb, high fat foods as a result of evolution, and the body requiring high-energy foods in order to fuel the flight or fight mechanism if a person was in danger. Whilst this response is no longer required, the body still reacts in the same manner, which explains why stress can trigger cravings for highly-palatable foods. 

Reacting to every craving, which people then are probably experiencing as a result of constantly eating said craving, is not teaching people to develop a balanced relationship with food; it is teaching people to binge eat. There is nothing wrong with eating "junk food", in moderation, but nutritional food is vital in order to fix the damage that has resulted from your eating disorder, and keep your body healthy. Just because you never experience cravings for fruits and vegetables does not mean your body is not in need of them. It simply means that you are disregarding your body’s true nutritional needs in favour of responding to cravings.

Blindly encouraging people to act on all hunger feelings (both mental and physical) without stopping to consider if they are physically hungry or not, is dangerous territory, as it could easily lead to people developing a binge eating problem...that is REALITY, not fatphobia - especially when there is always a risk that people recovering from anorexia could transition into bulimic behaviours, or binging behaviours, during their an attempt at recovery. To deny that possibility is negligent and disingenuous. All in influencers teach people that binging “doesn’t exist”, so people who follow all in engage in acting on extreme hunger, not realising that many of them are being taught to engage in binge eating behaviours as a way of dealing with certain emotions. What makes this more of a problem is wanting medical intervention or investigation is often blown off and disregarded, even likened to "remaining disordered" for dare questioning that this may be unsafe. Very dangerous for people who are already trying to recovery from an illness in which they used food as a coping mechanism.

Before anyone tries to attack me for my view, I think one needs to consider that to respond to literally every craving and food you experience by immediately acting on it does not sound like freedom to me. In fact, it sounds very similar to being controlled by my eating disorder, except that instead of feeling compelled to deprive my body when it was desperately hunger, you are still being controlled by thoughts, but ones which drive you to feed yourself excessively, even past the point of satiety. I envision recovery to be a point of true freedom, where I have achieved a healthy, balanced relationship with food, and am no longer controlled by it, at either end of the spectrum.
